results.why: A well-formed model whose declarations match its tensors. The most important case in the corpus: everything here is a false positive, and a scanner that reports anything has failed.

Declares F16 while every tensor is Q4_K. Precision drives memory, throughput and accuracy, so a quantized model presented as full precision misrepresents all three. This is the axis no scanner that only reads headers can see.
Declares 7 billion parameters and carries two million. Requires summing tensor shapes rather than trusting general.parameter_count.
A chat template that reaches for the interpreter. The template ships inside the metadata block and runs where the model is served.
TRAP. An ordinary Jinja chat template with loops and conditionals. Templates are normal; a scanner that flags every template is unusable on real models.
A protocol-2 pickle carrying a GLOBAL opcode, sitting next to a clean model. Found only by walking the directory, not by parsing the model file.
TRAP. A file named .pkl that is plain text. Extension-based detection reports it; reading the bytes does not. This is the exact failure mode published against picklescan.
config.json enables trust_remote_code, which runs code shipped with the weights.
TRAP. The key is present and false. Matching on the key name rather than the value reports it; that is a false positive on a correctly configured model.
config.json says float16 while the tensors are Q4_K. The declaration lives beside the model rather than inside it, so this needs both files read and reconciled.
